extract: Jio Platforms' grey market premium has surged 84% in two weeks, signalling rising interest in the telecom and digital services company's upcoming initial public offering.
The premium climbed to Rs 230 a share on October 16, from Rs 125 on October 3.
The latest grey market premium (GMP) represents a 20.6% premium over the IPO's upper price band of Rs 1,119 a share.
Reliance Jio IPO: India's largest-ever initial public offering (IPO) - Jio Platforms IPO - is set to open for public subscription on Wednesday, 21 October.
With a price band of ₹1,065– ₹1,119 per equity share, the company intends to raise between ₹28,755 crore and ₹30,213 crore through the public issue.
Jio IPO is a completely fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares.

Reliance Industries shares declined on Friday, October 16, reversing part of their recent gains as investors assessed the implications of the proposed initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the company's digital services subsidiary.
The Mukesh Ambani stock fell as much as 2.5% to an intraday low of ₹1,192.75 on the BSE, despite gaining around 5% over the preceding three sessions.
It was trading close to its 52-week low of ₹1,152.30, recorded in October 2026, and remained around 26% below its 52-week high of ₹1,611.20, hit in January 2026.
HDFC Bank shares were marginally higher on Friday, gaining 0.14 per cent to ₹727.90 on the NSE as of 1.09 IST, a day before the bank is set to announce its Q2FY27 results.
The stock opened at ₹727.90, touched an intraday high of ₹734.90 and a low of ₹726.05, against a previous close of ₹726.85.
Selling pressure was at its most intense this week, with 77.11 per cent of traded volume, 27,13,736 units, on the sell side, against just 22.89 per cent on the buy side.

Tata Steel has commissioned a series of advanced manufacturing facilities at its Kalinganagar plant and unveiled the expansion of Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited (NINL) in Odisha, involving a cumulative investment of around ₹9,067 crore.

The new facilities at Tata Steel Kalinganagar (TSK) include two continuous galvanising lines (CGLs) with a combined capacity of one million tonnes per annum (mtpa), a 0.9 mtpa continuous annealing line (CAL), Phase-I of a 7 mtpa slurry pipeline project

The company said the galvanising lines will enable Tata Steel to manufacture advanced automotive steel, including coated advanced high-strength steels (AHSS), catering to the requirements of automobile and appliance manufacturers.

The National Steering Committee on Friday reviewed the progress of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme and approved five Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs) worth ₹1,194.92 crore for ITI clusters in Maharashtra, Odisha and Jammu
Tata Steel Foundation, BVG India, Belrise Industries, Eagle Infra India and Inderdeep Infra India will partner in upgrading the five ITI clusters.
The cumulative investment approved under the PM-SETU scheme till now is to the tune of ₹3,687 crore, the agency said.
